articleTitle: Transmission Characteristics of Multiplexed OAM Beams in Time-Varying Non-Kolmogorov Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) of light has been used in optical communication to improve the capacity and spectral rate. However, OAM beams are distorted by atmospheric turbulence in free-space optical (FSO) communication link. In this paper, a propagation model of multiplexed OAM beams in time-varying non-Kolmogorov atmospheric turbulence is established here. Different from the time-varying Kolmogorov atmospheric turbulence model which only considers the ideal atmospheric turbulence, we consider the turbulence parameters of different atmospheres and the temporal and spatial variation in FSO communication link. Then the influences of time-varying non-Kolmogorov turbulence on characteristics of OAM beams are analyzed from the perspective of space, time domain and theoretical characteristic parameters of non-Kolmogorov turbulence.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Assisted Optical Fiber Vector Bending Sensor Based on MZI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: This paper presents a Mach-Zehnder interference-based axisymmetric misalignment structure and analyzes the curvature response in the 0°, 90°, and 180°. Breaking through the limitations of the wavelength linear fitting demodulation method, Support Vector Machine (SVM) can accurately distinguish between the three directions, meanwhile, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) can precisely predict the curvature magnitude in each direction with the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) only 0.021 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. With the assistance of machine learning algorithms, simultaneous and accurate demodulation of both vector and curvature is achieved.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of 32-Channel C-Band Digital Transmitter/Receiver Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: This paper describes the successful development of a modular, integrated, high-efficiency, and multi-functional 32-channel C-band digital transmitter/receiver (T/R) module based on C-band high-power GaN power amplifier chips and system-in-package (SIP) technology. The signal processing board uses a field-programmable gate array as its core device in combination with high-speed analog-to-digital converter (ADC) and digital-to-analog converter (DAC) devices, and by using the JESD204B high-speed interface, functions including ADC synchronization, DAC synchronization, and data transmission synchronization have been designed and implemented. The module has functions that include independent control of transmission and reception, numerical control of phase shifting and attenuation, and module self-checking. Test results indicate that the T/R module offers advantages such as a wide bandwidth, high output power, low fabrication cost, and great universality for applications.

articleTitle: Research of Raft Algorithm Improvement in Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Blockchain has the characteristics of decentralisation, security, reliability and non-tampering, and its core is to reach consensus reliably and quickly through a suitable consensus mechanism. The Raft consensus algorithm in blockchain has advantages such as high performance and high availability, which is suitable for asset management business, but the existing Raft algorithm improvement strategy still has the problems of possible voting divergence and insufficient consideration of malicious node shielding, so the paper proposes a Raft algorithm election improvement scheme and potential malicious node defence improvement scheme, which has more rigorous logic, and is able to reduce the election failure rate, verify the correctness of the leader node, for all the malicious nodes in the system can be accurately identified and shielded, to protect the security of the system, so that the Raft algorithm has a wider range of applications.

articleTitle: Usability Evaluation of the Mobile Automated Fingerprint Identification System Using the PACMAD Model: An Empirical Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: This study evaluates the usability of the Mobile Automated Fingerprint Identification System (MAFIS) mobile application within Philippine law enforcement using the PACMAD model. The objectives include assessing effectiveness, efficiency, learnability, memorability, error frequency, and cognitive load. A mixed-methods approach was employed, involving questionnaire surveys and usability tests with 21 participants from the Crime Laboratory - Fingerprint Identification Division. Results indicate highly positive perceptions of the MAFIS application across all usability attributes, with weighted mean scores consistently falling within the “Highly Acceptable” range. Qualitative findings highlight user satisfaction with interface design and features, alongside desired improvements for enhanced functionality. These insights inform the optimization of the MAFIS application to support law enforcement efforts, contributing to more effective crime prevention and public safety in the Philippines.

articleTitle: LSTM-Autoencoder For Faster-Than-Nyquist Optical Wireless MIMO Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) technology introduces additional inter-symbol interference (ISI), which significantly impacts the bit error rate (BER) performance of FTN multiple input multiple output (MIMO) optical wireless communication (OWC) system. To address this issue, an end-to-end (E2E) FTN-MIMO OWC system utilizing a long short-term memory (LSTM) autoencoder has been proposed. This approach effectively eliminates the influence of ISI and achieves complete signal recovery. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposal improves BER performance to different degrees under various conditions compared to conventional systems using maximum likelihood (ML) mothed. Specifically, with acceleration factors of 0.9 and 0.8, our proposal demonstrates an improvement in BER performance by 1.6dB and 2.2dB respectively, effectively mitigating the complex mixed ISI caused by FTN shaping and atmospheric turbulence channel.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction Method of Active Echo Highlight Structure Based on Transformer Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Physical feature extraction of underwater acoustic targets is crucial for target detection and identification, which is able to transform the physical properties of targets into quantifiable feature parameters. Structure extraction is performed by statistically analyzing some characteristics in the target echo signal, such as the number of highlights, intensity distribution, time interval. Traditional highlight structure extraction methods rely on manually designed signal processing techniques. However, these methods often face challenges in maintaining extraction accuracy under complex environmental noise. Deep learning methods effectively solve these problems by constructing multilayer neural networks to automatically learn feature representations from the data. To address the above issues, this paper proposes a feature extraction method for active echo highlight structure based on a Transformer network. The underwater acoustic target-echo highlight model has been designed. Furthermore, a deep learning model was constructed based on Transformer to achieve patch embedding and feature extraction of the input samples. Moreover, a joint loss function, including the regression loss of echo highlight structure, the regression loss of target scale, and the time extension correction loss, was designed to improve the convergence effect of the model and the accuracy of feature extraction. The model training results show that the prediction error of the number of highlights can be controlled within 5, and the prediction error of the target scale is controlled within 12 meters. In addition, the model is tested on actual underwater acoustic target echo data, and achieves a good prediction performance of the highlight structure on real target echoes.

articleTitle: Experimental 100M Real-Time Visible Light Communication System Based on Miniaturized Laser Drived
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Aiming at the demand for equipment miniaturisation for underwater optical communication, this paper designs a blue-green laser driver circuit that can realise arbitrary waveform driving. Using the chip-type current feedback operational amplifier THS3091, which replaces the large-size RF amplifier module, together with the constant current source and Bias-T, the miniaturisation of the laser driver circuit is achieved. Based on OSRAM PL520B and PL450B laser tubes, an arbitrary waveform driver with a 3dB bandwidth of 70MHz is realised, while the average output optical power of PL520B is 45.6mW, and that of PL450B is 120.6mW, and the overall power supply is only 2.4 W. Finally, using the miniaturised arbitrary waveform laser driver in this paper, a 100Mbps real-time laser modulation circuit based on OFDM is completed. modulation of 100Mbps real-time visible light communication system experiment is built.

articleTitle: Hard X-ray Detector Based on p-Si/i-MgO/n-TiO2 Heterojunction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Wide bandgap semiconductor-based directconversion X-ray detectors present a multitude of benefits and hold significant promise for various applications. In this study, a direct-conversion X-ray detector utilizing a p-Si/i-MgO/n-TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> structure was fabricated using radio frequency magnetron sputtering. The X-ray detection properties of the device were systematically investigated. This device achieved a signal-to-noise ratio and sensitivity of 58.75 and 1048.6 nC/(Gy<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">air</inf>•cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), respectively, under a 6 MV hard X-ray and a bias voltage of -1 V, which was 359% and 273% higher than the p-Si/n-TiO2 structure devices. Furthermore, the p-Si/i-MgO/n-TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> X-ray detector has a faster response time of 0.11 s (rise) and 0.04 s (decay). These results provide new ideas for the subsequent development of highperformance wide-bandgap semiconductor hard X-ray detectors.

articleTitle: MHSA-CNN-Bi-LSTM Based Interference Cancellation Algorithm for MIMO-FTN-OWC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In MIMO-FTN-OWC systems, inter-symbol interference (ISI) caused by the fast-than-Nyquist (FTN) technique is a significant issue. To address this problem, we propose an ISI cancellation algorithm a hybrid network consisting of MHSA-CNN-Bi-LSTM. This algorithm effectively eliminates ISI by leveraging the feature extraction capability of CNN, the bi-directional sequence information capture capability of Bi-LSTM, and the multi-head self-attention (MHSA) mechanism. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposal achieves improved bit error rate (BER) performance compared to traditional algorithms without deep learning-based ISI cancellation, with a maximum improvement of 7 dB under various conditions. Furthermore, when operating within the Mazo limit for acceleration factor, our algorithm successfully eliminates the FTN caused ISI and achieves BER performance comparable to that of orthogonal systems.

articleTitle: Sagnac Type Fiber Optic Current Sensor Based on a Single Circularly Polarized Fiber and a 3*3 Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The impact of input light polarization on the demodulation results in the 3×3 coupler-based current demodulation scheme is analyzed. By utilizing the features of a single circularly polarized optical fiber, this influence can be eliminated.

articleTitle: Ga2O3/GaN/Ga2O3 N-P-N Double-Junction Ultraviolet Photodetector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/GaN/Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> n-p-n double-junction ultraviolet (UV) photodetector was successfully fabricated by radio frequency magnetron sputtering. The device exhibits stable responses under 265 nm UV irradiation at -3 V bias, with a responsivity of ~130 mA/W, an external quantum efficiency of ~61%, a detectivity of ~8.21×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> Jones, which are 3.4, 3.4, and 8 times that of the GaN/Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> p-n type device, respectively. The energy band diagram shows that due to the large valence band offset of Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and GaN, large number of holes accumulate at the Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/GaN interface closer to the cathode, which reduce the valence band offset at the junction to promote the transmission of photogenerated carriers and improve the device performance.

articleTitle: A Doppler Rate Estimation-Based Frequency Hopping Carrier Tracking Algorithm in LEO Satellite-Ground Link
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Frequency hopping has good anti-interference ability. However, the high-speed movement between Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite and ground will lead to a large Doppler frequency of the received signal carrier. With the switching of the frequency hopping frequency point, the Doppler frequency will change abruptly, which will affect the subsequent signal demodulation. To solve this problem, a carrier tracking loop algorithm based on normalized Doppler rate estimation is proposed. The loop separates the frequency hopping agility factor from the phase and persistently locks the continuous Doppler rate. When the signal is detected to have high power interference at some frequency points, the algorithm performs delay locking to shield the disturbance to the tracking loop. The simulation results and analysis show that compared with the traditional phase-locked loop, the proposed algorithm can be well applied to frequency hopping carrier tracking in large Doppler dynamic and harsh interference environment.

articleTitle: Attention-Enhanced Ensemble Learning for Diabetic Retinopathy Classification with Interpretability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is a severe complication of diabetes that significantly impacts vision and can potentially lead to blindness. The effective diagnosis and timely treatment of DR is crucial preventing vision loss. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have emerged as a prominent tool in the field of medical image analysis for this purpose. This paper proposes a novel ensemble residual deep learning model that integrates parallel convolutional filters with shallow convolutional neural network enhanced by a channel attention mechanism for the classification of DR. The proposed model leverages the strength of residual learning and attention mechanism to improve feature extraction and classification performance. To validate the effectiveness of the model, this study conducted extensive experiment on DR data, where the model demonstrated robust diagnostic capabilities. The results were remarkable, achieving accuracy of 97.69<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, F1-score of 97.77<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, sensitivity of 97.02 %, specificity of 98.18%, precision and recall both at 97.77%. Furthermore, the model attained an area under curve of 98%, highlighting its potential to serve as an effective supplementary tool for the analysis of DR images. These findings underscore the model's potential to assist healthcare professionals in the early and accurate diagnosis of DR, ultimately contributing to better patient outcome.

articleTitle: All Fiber Electric Field Sensor Based on Electrical Control of Liquid Crystal Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: An electric field (E-field) sensor based on liquid crystal (LC) infiltrated photonic crystal fiber (PCF) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated in this paper. Liquid crystals (5CB nematic liquid crystals, NLC) are filled into the cladding air holes of a PCF. A photonic bandgap type waveguide is then formed. Applying an external E-field to the NLC-filled PCF changes the alignment of the LC molecules in the LC layer, which affects the edge wavelength of the photonic bandgap. The E-field sensitivity is about 157.51 nm/kV/mm in the range of 130 V to 220 V (0.65 kV/mm to 1.1 kV/mm). The sensor is lightweight, low-cost, sensitive, and stable, and can be widely used in industrial production.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient and Ultrabroadband Hybrid Silicon-Lithium Niobate Grating Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: We propose and design a highly efficient and ultrabroadband grating coupler based on the hybrid Silicon and Lithium Niobate platform. By using a triple layer structure and a bottom metal reflector, simulation results demonstrate that the minimal insertion loss is about −0.15dB and the 1-dB optical bandwidth is up to 135 nm. Such a broadband and highly-efficient grating coupler is suitable for various thin film Lithium Niobate devices.

articleTitle: Four New Optimal Codes over F7 and F9
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of constructing an optimallinear code is considered. Four new codes with parameters [18,12,6], [21,16,5] over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_{9}$</tex>, [20,15,5], [19,14,5] over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{F}_{7}$</tex> are determined. Their generator matrices and weight distributions are presented and these four linear codes are new and have better parameters than the known results.

articleTitle: A Ground Application System for On-Orbit Servicing Satellite Based on OODA Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The ground application system is a significant component of a space program, which could provide the services of mission planning, satellite data processing, scene displays, et al. Due to the separation between the uplink operation control and the downlink data processing, the current ground application system could hardly follow the On-Orbit Servicing (OOS) satellite's application requirements, including the variety task types, complicated application scenario and closely interrelationship between the satellite and the ground. Based on the OODA (Observation, Orientation, Decision, Action) loop, a new ground application system for the OOS satellite is proposed. By using the reasoning and self-decision techniques, the OOS satellite operational requirements are automatically generated from the data processing results, which makes a close-loop between the satellite and the ground. The feasibility of the proposed ground application system is verified by a practical OOS space program.

articleTitle: Two Classes of Optimal Frequency Hopping Sequences with New Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Frequency hopping sequences (FHSs) play a crucial role in wireless communication, while Reed-Solomon (RS) codes hold a good algebraic structure. In this paper, two classes of FHSs are constructed from punctured RS codes, both containing new parameters. The two classes of FHSs both meet the lower bound of peak nontrivial Hamming correlation given by (3), and under certain constraints both classes can meet the upper bound of set size given by (2). Moreover, the methods in this paper can be regarded as a generalization of some previous methods.

articleTitle: New Lower Bounds on Aperiodic Hamming Correlation of Frequency Hopping Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: It is generally accepted that aperiodic Hamming correlation of frequency hopping sequences (FHSs) matters especially in practical communication applications. In this paper, new lower bounds of FHS sets on AHC is proposed. Then the performance of our new bounds are compared with some existing lower bounds both by theoretical deduction and simulation. Results show that our new bounds make an effective improvement on the previous bounds.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Characterization of Optoelectronic Devices by Pilot-Assisted Harmonic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: A high-frequency characterizing method is proposed for measuring frequency response parameters of optoelectronic devices through pilot-assisted harmonic analysis. The frequency response of the electro-optic modulator (EOM) can be extracted by the pilot insertion and extraction fixed at low frequency. The frequency response of the photodetector (PD) can be solved by subtracting the modulation response of EOM from the harmonic components in the photocurrent signal. In the experimental demonstration, an EOM is measured with a fixed-low-frequency pilot signal at 70 MHz, and the frequency response of a commercial PD is evaluated up to 50 GHz by expanding the measuring frequency range up to a 2-fold driving frequency range.

articleTitle: Realization of Underwater Wireless Optical Communication with high Alignment Accuracy Based on All-optical Acquisition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In this paper, we present an underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) system with high alignment accuracy based on all-optical acquisition. The system adopts all-optical acquisition technology to achieve underwater acquisition pointing tracking (APT) for rapid establishment of UWOC links and variable divergence angle technology to achieve stable data transmission of UWOC. By this way, the alignment accuracy can be controlled within 1 mrad when the link is established. Thus, the UWOC systems can reduce the laser beam divergence angle to 1mrad for minimizing the intensity loss. So when applied in Jerlov I seawater with 17dBm of transmitting optical power, the underwater equivalent transmission distance can reach more than 150 meters, where the UWOC link can be automatically established and the bit error rate (BER) value can still be zero with a data rate of 1Mbps.

articleTitle: Package Number Detection Method Based on Improved YOLOv5 in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Hot metal can not fall to the ground is the most important requirement in the steel plant hot metal scheduling project. The identification of the hanging tank/sitting tank and the packet number of the molten iron tank is the most critical in the process, and the final decision is left to the manual. Due to the chaotic environmental background, complex lighting conditions, high temperature and high pressure, loud noise, heavy dust, non-standard spraying of iron can bag number, serious wear, paint off and other problems, the detection environment is extremely harsh, making conventional methods ineffective, detection results become extremely unreliable, affecting manual interpretation and decision-making, and the production accident rate increases sharply. As a convenient, fast and easy to deploy network detection model, Yolov5 has been favored by many researchers. However, due to the complex environment of our project, the conventional Yolov5 target detection accuracy is poor, the robustness is poor, and false detection often occurs. Although many researchers have proposed different Yolov5 target detection models, however, when the improved model is applied to our complex environment, the results are not improved, and problems still exist. In response to the above problems, This paper proposes an improved YOLOv5 algorithm to address the challenges of detecting the status of molten iron ladles and recognizing packet numbers in complex scenes. The model has been improved in three aspects: ① Replacing the original YOLOv5 convolution module with the GSConv module (Grouped Shuffle Convolution). This significantly reduces the computational load, meeting the real-time requirements of visual detection in molten iron dispatching, and addresses the difficulty of the original model in effectively extracting target features due to poor imaging quality under harsh production conditions. ② Replacing the FPN (Feature Pyramid Network) structure with BiFPN (Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network). This allows the model to fuse features at different scales, improving the detection and recognition rate of targets under poor imaging conditions. ③ Adding the CoordAtt (Coordinate Attention) module. This enhances the model's ability to focus on different positions on the feature map, further improving the detection and recognition rate of targets in complex imaging conditions. Comparative experiments founded on real data disclosed that, as opposed to other methods, the proffered approach attains superior target detection accuracy with conspicuously reduced parameters and a lightweight model. Furthermore, it manifests outstanding generalization ability, substantiating that our targeted network optimizations are efficacious and can satisfy the operational requisites of real-world applications, presenting considerable practical value.

articleTitle: A Multidimensional Node Selection Method Towards MOAS Outsourcing Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Multiple Origin AS (MOAS) outsourcing mitigation is a defense countermeasure against prefix hijacking, during which the mitigation AS attracts and redirects the hijacked traffic to the legitimate origin AS by announcing the hijacked prefix. In order to enhance the effectiveness of mitigation, this paper proposes a node selection method for the mitigation AS. Specially, it takes multiple dimensions of AS topology into considerations: the hierarchical type, the Internet eXchange Point (IXP) access and the neighbor relationships of the AS. Experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve better mitigation effect against prefix hijacking compared other methods.

articleTitle: Image Processing Algorithm Assisted Optical Lithography Processing for the Fabrication of Photonic Chips
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: We demonstrate a measurement methodology for improving the photonic chip fabrication based on an image processing algorithm, where the chips with fabrication errors can be maintained within 0.22 µm via university-level optical photolithography.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Large Language Models in Programming Tutoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The appearance of large language models (LLMs) and related products has generated widespread attention and lively discussions in both industry and academia. Given their extensive applications and remarkable achievements in numerous fields, LLMs have rapidly emerged as a frontier research topic that is actively explored by numerous scholars. This paper delves into the application and current research status of LLMs in the field of programming tutoring. Firstly, we outline the applicability of LLMs in programming tutoring, emphasizing the new opportunities brought by their powerful language understanding and generation capabilities to programming education. Subsequently, through empirical research, we validate the effectiveness of LLMs in correcting programming errors. The research results have confirmed the effectiveness of LLMs in bug localization and program repair, demonstrating the significant potential and practical value of large language models in Programming Tutoring Systems. By continuously optimizing model performance, we can further advance the development of programming education.

articleTitle: BVR-AD: Bridging Virtual and Real for Autonomous Driving with Environment Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In the realm of autonomous driving, bridging the gap between virtual simulations and real-world environments remains a critical challenge. This paper introduces BVR-AD, an advanced framework that employs environment adaptation techniques to integrate virtual and real driving data into a unified semantic space. By leveraging generative adversarial networks (GANs), BVR-AD facilitates the transfer of learned driving knowledge across different environments, thereby enhancing model robustness and applicability. The proposed method focuses on maintaining the semantic integrity of key driving elements, such as lanes, pedestrians, roads, and buildings, across both virtual and real environments. Extensive evaluations on diverse datasets, including Airsim, Udacity, and CARLA, demonstrate BVR-AD's capability to achieve significant performance gains and improved interpretability in autonomous driving tasks. Our results highlight the model's effectiveness in ensuring that representations learned in simulated environments are transferable and effective in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Design of 450nm Gallium Nitride-Based Distributed Feedback Laser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: GaN-based distributed feedback (DFB) lasers are promising for visible light communications. This paper reports the design of laterally-corrugated ridge-waveguide DFB LD without an epitaxial re-growth. The factors that determine the effective coupling coefficient have been investigated.

articleTitle: Reliability Performance of RIS-CR-NOMA Based Short-Packet Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Considering the potential of integrating reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) with cognitive radio (CR) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems in the Internet of Things (IoT), this paper investigates the reliability performance of a downlink RIS-assisted CR-NOMA network with short packet communications. To characterize the performance, the closed-form expressions of average block error rate (BLER) at primary and secondary users are derived. The theoretical analysis is verified through simulation results. The achieved results demonstrate that the proposed RIS aided overlay CR-NOMA network is advantageous in short packet communication, which has great potential for IoT applications.

articleTitle: A Formal Specification Approach to Specify Pet's House System Using Z - Notations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The formal method (FM) is an innovative method that employs mathematical notations to describe explicit and precise requirements. This makes it possible to find errors and conflicts early in the software development process. To improve quality, the Z concept can assist with system specifications, design, and testing. A formal Specifications of a pet system is presented in this paper using the Z specification language. The complicated pet system is in charge of maintaining information about pets, owners, and numerous components of their care. We demonstrate how the requirements of the pet system, including its functionality, data structures, and behavior, can be specified using Z. In this specification, we aim to highlight the benefits of using formal methods to ensure the accuracy and reliability of complex systems and to show how valuable they are in system design and development. Formal approaches are advantageous not just for mission-critical systems, but also in commercial and business-oriented applications, since they could significantly decrease development time, verification, and maintenance costs. These results will serve as motivation for formal approaches.

articleTitle: Silicon-Nitride Temperature Sensor with Enhanced Sensitivity Based on Mach-Zehnder Interferometer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: We demonstrate broadband Silicon-Nitride asymmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer temperature sensor showing near 40 pm/K sensitivity from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$85^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}$</tex> in S+C+L band, which is two times larger than conventional Silicon-Nitride temperature sensors. The proposed sensor only needs single lithography for the sensing unit, without introducing negative thermo-optic coefficient (TOC) materials. In addition, Optical properties of the sensor are accurately extracted from the optical measurement method.

articleTitle: A Deep Neural Network for Simultaneous Channel Estimation and Signal Detection in MIMO-OFDM-FSO System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The complex receiver and limited performance of Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) Free Space Optical (FSO) communication systems are addressed by employing a Deep Neural Networks (DNN) for channel estimation and detection tasks. The DNN learns the mapping relationship between the atmospheric turbulence channel's complex characteristics and the signals through extensive data processing, enabling joint channel estimation and detection. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibit enhanced robustness, superior generalization performance compared to traditional detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Comparison of Prefilter for DDFSE Equalized Fast-Than-Nyquist Signaling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Fast-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling improves spectrum efficiency (SE) by compressing the symbol interval and is a promising communication scheme. However, high compression rate means serious inter-symbol interference (ISI), so researchers have been exploring various low-complexity and efficient equalization methods. Delayed feedback sequence estimation (DDFSE) achieves a good tradeoff between complexity and equalization effect, and can achieve better equalization effect with a prefilter, but no one has compared which prefilter has the best BER performance for FTN signaling. We proposed a new prefilter based on unbiased maximum signal-to-interference-to-noise ratio (U-SINR) prefilter and mean square whitened matched filter (MS-WMF), and compared it with three other prefilters to find the best prefilter for medium and low time-squeezing factors. The simulation results show that in the vast majority of cases, we recommend MS-WMF, but new prefilter can be used to obtain better equalization effects when the signal-to-noise ratio is high and the time-squeezing factors is low.

articleTitle: Vernier-Effect-Based Fiber Microcoupler for Salinity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: A highly sensitive fiber optic multimode coupler for salinity measurement based on Vernier effect is proposed. The coupler is manufactured by tapering two single-mode optical fiber whose sides touch each other. By controlling the shape of the coupler in the waist region, the enveloped interference spectrum caused by the Vernier effect can be observed. Compared with the common interference spectrum of a coupler, this enveloped spectrum exhibits a higher refractive index sensitivity. The experimental results show that the sample of this coupler could achieve a salinity sensitivity of 1.742nm/%o in the measurement range from 0% o to 50% o, and the magnification factor is about 2.93. This high-sensitivity, low-cost coupler can be applied to salinity or refractive index related measurements in industrial and marine fields.

articleTitle: A Low Differential Modal Gain All-Fiber Few-Mode Erbium-Doped Fiber Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: We developed a low differential modal gain (DMG) all-fiber few-mode erbium-doped fiber amplifier(FM-EDFA), which supports the transmissions of four signal modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{LP}_{01}$</tex>, LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{LP}_{21}$</tex>, LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf>) and features a high energy utilization rate. At 1550 nm, the gain of each mode is greater than 22 dB, and the DMG is lower than 1.63 dB. While the average gain of each mode in the C-band is greater than 21 dB, and the DMG is only 2.38 dB.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Intercluster Transmission in Wireless Sensor Networks Deploying Discrete Power Splitters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In energy-constrained clustered wireless sensor networks (WSNs), communication between cluster heads often utilizes cooperative simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) techniques to enhance data transmission energy efficiency. This paper focuses on maximizing the cooperative transmission energy efficiency between two cluster heads equipped with low-cost and low-complexity discrete power splitters. In such cases, discrete power splitting ratios lead to a non-convex optimization issue for resource allocation. We propose an algorithm based on a variable-dimension expansion method to effectively find the optimal power transmission and harvesting energy allocation policies. Numerical experiment findings confirm the proposed DSNRA algorithm's convergence and superiority under the impact of power splitting resolutions and maximum transmit power.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Measuring Method of Depolarizer Characteristic Parameters in Depolarized Fiber Optic Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The output spectrum of Sagnac interferometer assembly of depolarized fiber optic gyroscope (DFOG) was modeled and the results of simulation and experiment show that the output spectrum is the coherently modulated spectrum of incident broadband source. The self-correlation curves of the coherently modulated spectrum were calculated and it was found that the position and amplitude of self-correlation peaks are determined by the length of PMFs and the intersection angle between the polarization axes of two polarization maintaining fibers at joint points. Then, a measuring method of depolarizer characteristic parameters is proposed and investigated theoretically and experimentally and the length of the PMFs and the angular deviation of the depolarizer are measured. The proposed method has high sensitivity and provides an effective method for monitoring and evaluating the parameters of the depolarizer in DFOG.

articleTitle: A Strain Measurement Method on the Upper Surface of Basin Insulator Based on OFDR Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In this paper, a method for the detection of strain in basin insulators is proposed. The system is based on a sensing fiber, which is fixed on the surface of a basin insulator. An interrogator measures the backscattered light from the sensing fiber, which varies with strain. The method enables strain measurements of 2.6 m with a spatial resolution of 1 mm, or 2600 sensing points. The strain is measured with a resolution of 5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\varepsilon$</tex> and a linearity of 0.9998, and the whole system corresponds to a measurement time of 2 seconds. The method provides a simple and fast idea for insulator strain detection.

articleTitle: High Precision Micro - Dispersion Measurement Based on Spectral Interferometry using a Soliton Microcomb
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of the diff - iteration method based on spectral interferometry for measuring the micro - dispersion of optical devices (optical fiber, lens, etc.). Using an optical frequency comb, based on the phase demodulation of dispersion interference spectrum, by employing the carefully designed diff - iteration method to solve the dispersion curve at any position and any order. Our approach is proficient in precisely measuring micro - dispersion across a broadband spectrum, without the need for cumbersome wavelength scanning processes or reliance on complex high - repetition - rate combs, while enabling adjustable resolution. The efficacy of the proposed method is validated through simulations and experiments. The approach ensures high precision, while maintaining a simple system structure, with realizing adjustable resolution, thereby propelling the practical implementation of precise measurement and control - dispersion.

articleTitle: Actively Mode-Locked Optoelectronic Oscillator with Independently-Tunable Pulse Width and Repetition Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: A method for independently tuning the pulse width and the repetition frequency of the microwave pulse train generated by an actively mode-locked optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The innovation of this scheme is that the driving signal applied to the mode-locking device is not a conventional sinusoidal signal, but an amplitude-modulated signal. In such a case, with an appropriate setting of the loop gain, microwave pulse is generated only at the maximum amplitude of the driving waveform. Consequently, the carrier frequency of the driving signal regulates the pulse width, and its amplitude modulation frequency controls the repetition frequency. An experiment is carried out to verify the feasibility of the proposed method. In the experiment, three microwave pulse trains with a fixed repetition frequency of 179.64 kHz and pulse widths from 510 ns to 125 ns are generated. In addition, two microwave pulse trains with an identical pulse width of 125 ns and repetition frequencies of 359.28 kHz and 718.56 kHz are generated. This scheme greatly enhances the controllability of the mode-locked pulse train from an OEO, and also paves a way to generate ultra-short microwave pulses.

articleTitle: A Method for Modeling Normal User Behavior Based on Security Risk Audit Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In the field of data security audit, most current studies are confined to specific data sources, which are diverse and span across various industries. The heterogeneity of data sources results in significant differences in the generated audit data, thus impacting the cross-source reuse of audit methods. Furthermore, although progress has been made by these studies, there are still shortcomings in terms of audit comprehensiveness and coverage. To address these issues, this paper constructs a library of security risk audit elements to standardize the data processing of different sources, generating high-quality audit data that can cover a wider range of risk scenarios. The improvement in audit scenario coverage is shown through comparative analysis. Additionally, this paper also demonstrates a method for modeling normal user behavior with this library. Using the k-means algorithm, user behavior data from the Confluence backend was clustered. The clustering results, defined artificially, closely matched users' normal habits, proving the effectiveness of our elements-based method for modeling normal user behavior.

articleTitle: High-Efficient Resource Allocation Based on Deep Q-Network Enhanced Federated Learning in Slicing Packet Network for 5G ToB Service
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: We propose a computing power scheduling algorithm based on Deep Q-Network enhanced federated learning in Slicing Packet Network. Experimental demonstration and numerical evaluation show its overall feasibility and efficiency.

articleTitle: Minimum and Maximum Strong Diameters of the Strong Product of Cycles and Paths
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In interconnected networks, networks with smaller strong diameters tend to have better fault tolerance. This is because when the strong diameter of the network is small, the vertices are more closely connected and the path of information propagation is shorter, making it easier for the network to maintain communication and functionality in the event of an attack or failure. Whereas, when the strong diameter is large, the vertices are more distantly connected and the information propagation path is longer, which increases the vulnerability of the network and makes it more susceptible to attacks or failures. Therefore, strong diameter is one of the key metrics to measure and optimize the fault tolerance performance of the network. In this paper, a strong product network of cycles and paths is constructed by strong product and the strong diameter of this network is investigated. Specifically, we determine the minimum strong diameter of the strong product of even cycles and paths, and the upper and lower bounds of the minimum strong diameter of the strong product of odd cycles and paths. In addition, we give a lower bound on the maximum strong diameter of the strong product of cycles and paths, and present a conjecture on the maximum strong diameter of the strong product graph of cycles and paths.

articleTitle: High-Precision Synchronization Using Laser-Based Free Space Time Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The high-precision time synchronization is very important to the fundamental scientific research and engineering application. A scheme of synchronization with laser-based free-space time transfer is presented. A time signal produced by a continuous wave (CW) laser is transferred over a 120 m free-space link. An hundred picosecond-level time synchronization between transmitter and receiver is realized with a time delay correction technique. A synchronization experiment shows an absolute time delay of 480 ns is improved to be 300 ps with an active time delay correction. The time stability is below 40 ps at 1 s and below 20 ps over 10 s, respectively. This experimental results prove that this scheme is effective for high-precision time transfer and synchronization over free-space link.

articleTitle: Research on Sparse Remote Sensing Matching Method Based on LoFTR Descriptor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: As an important means of obtaining information about the Earth's surface, remote sensing mapping is widely used in fields such as military, environmental monitoring, resource surveying, and disaster monitoring. Consequently, remote sensing image matching has always been a prominent area of research in image matching. Optical images closely align with human visual perception of the world, but they are susceptible to environmental influences, which can result in information loss or operational failure. LoFTR, as a dense matching model, is limited by its complexity and is not suitable for most equipment conditions. Therefore, this paper proposes a sparse remote sensing matching method based on the LoFTR descriptor, which utilizes RIFT feature points to extract the corresponding LoFTR feature map to obtain the corresponding feature descriptors, and performs registration by calculating cosine similarity. In the experiments, multiple sets of Optical and SAR remote sensing images were used as test data. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively retains the advantages of LoFTR, reduces the model's complexity and parameter scale, and achieves good results in remote sensing image registration for both Optical and SAR types, with sub-pixel registration accuracy.

articleTitle: New Classes of Optimal Wide-Gap One-Coincidence Frequency Hopping Sequence Sets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce new classes of wide-gap one-coincidence frequency hopping sequence (WG-OC-FHS) sets, crucial for achieving anti-jamming capabilities in frequency hopping communication systems. Our construction optimally utilizes the available frequencies to create wide-gap between adjacent frequency slots. Designed sequence sets are optimal according to both the WG-Peng-Fan Bound and the WG-Lempel-Greenberger Bound. Moreover, our method represents a generalization of some approaches proposed previously, offering expanded capabilities in generating diverse frequency hopping sequence (FHS) sets under identical parameters.

articleTitle: Mode Switch and Modulator in Strip Loaded Few-Mode Waveguide Formed on Slab Thin-Film Lithium Niobate on Insulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: We propose an optical mode switch and modulator based on hybrid polymer few-mode waveguide and slab thin-film lithium niobate waveguide, which enables efficient mode conversion and optical modulation at low voltages and wide wavelength range.

articleTitle: TrustPIoT: Blockchain-based Anonymous Authentication for Cross-Domain Intelligent PIoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Power Internet of Things (PIoT) is a crucial technology for smart grids, and it also plays a momentous role in current electric power data transmission and sharing. Currently, an increasing demand for cross-domain interactions requires various devices belonging to different domains to cooperate, which makes traditional identity authentication mechanisms unsuitable to ensure information security and privacy during communication. In addition, centralized power IoT systems will also face concerns of single point of failure, data tampering, etc. To tackle these issues, we design TrustPIoT, a blockchain-assisted authentication scheme for cross-domain PIoT, which achieves access control between cross-domain devices while ensuring identity anonymity. We exploit an on-chain and off-chain storage mechanism to ensure the consistency of the data, by introducing a cloud server to coordinate with the blockchain network. To verify its validity, we also conduct experiments on Hyperledger Fabric to evaluate the performance of TrustPIoT.

articleTitle: A Simulation Model of Control System for a Lightweight Space Active Mirror
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: This paper presents a conceptual design for the hardware implementation of a space Active Optics mirror assembly with active supports, allowing for precise shape and pointing control. The design includes actuator stacks arranged within the back ribs of the lightweight mirror, along with collocated force sensors that monitor changes in internal transfer forces, facilitating the reconstruction of the mirror's shape. Additionally, a fundamental control strategy is proposed for the hierarchical control of the mirror assembly, aimed at future large space telescopes.

articleTitle: Channel Reconstruction and Path Loss Characterization of Indoor T-Corridors based on Intelligent Reflecting Surface at 300GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The unique nature of the high frequencies in the terahertz band (0.1-10 terahertz) makes it impractical to use lower frequency channel models. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop new channel models to realize the potential of terahertz communications, and a variety of channel measurement methods and measurement environments can accelerate development efforts. Since Intelligent Reflective Surface (IRS) is a potential solution to improve the cost-effectiveness and energy efficiency of sixth generation (6G) wireless communication systems. Therefore, this paper presents a method to implement IRS functionality in a 3D ray-tracing simulator and applies it to a novel indoor T-corridor scenario with no line-of-sight path (NLoS) between the transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx). High-resolution 3D measurements are processed at 300 GHz to obtain bidirectional angular delay power spectra as well as delay and angular power distributions, and finally the channel is characterized by path loss. Numerical results show that the incorporation of IRS into wireless communication systems in this scenario can significantly improve the coverage and provide useful insights for optimizing the deployment of IRS in indoor T-corridor scenarios.

articleTitle: Adaptive Optical Power of Atmospheric Laser Communication based on Reciprocity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Free space optical communication, characterized by its high carrier frequency, strong directionality, and enhanced security, offers significant advantages for high-speed communication between buildings in smart cities. However, atmospheric turbulence disrupts the wavefront of propagating beams, severely impacting the stability and transmission rate of communication systems. In this paper, we propose an optical signal stabilized amplitude transmission method based on atmospheric turbulence channel reciprocity. This method aims to enhance the performance of atmospheric wireless optical communication systems by adaptively pre-compensating transmit power using real-time collected fading characteristic signals.

articleTitle: Optimal Client Selection for Wireless Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In order to address the issue of statistical heterogeneity in wireless federated learning, we proposed a novel client selection method. We introduced a new metric called client quality, which takes into account the local data volume of clients and the testing accuracy of the previous round's model. Based on this, we proposed a client selection method called Client Quality-based Client Selection (CQCS) to improve the performance of wireless federated learning. Results show that the proposed CQCS client selection method effectively enhances the global accuracy of the model. Specifically, compared to the baseline algorithms FedAvg, FedProx, and Per-FedAvg, the model average accuracy improved by 6.7%, 4.8%, and 3.1%, respectively, on the MNIST dataset. On the Cifar10 dataset, the model average accuracy improved by 3.4 %,3.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and 3.9%, respectively. Similarly, on the Fashion-MNIST dataset, the model average accuracy improved by 3.1 %, 3.8%, and 4.2%, respectively.

articleTitle: High Precision Distance Measurement of Micro-Motion Targets Based on FMCW LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) light detection and ranging (LiDAR) is considered as one of the most promising 3D imaging technologies by virtue of its single-photon detection sensitivity, high interference immunity, and high precision. However, due to the micro-motion of the target caused by the environment, a Doppler frequency shift is introduced into the beat frequency signal, which results in measurement inaccuracies. To solve this problem, we propose a dual sweep FMCW LiDAR system and a high precision distance measurement method for micro-motion targets, which can be applied in both active and passive environments. In the former, a 62-fold improvement in range precision could be achieved, and in the latter, the standard deviation of the measurement reached 11 µm.

articleTitle: Exploring Usability and User Experience in WeBarangay: A SUS and UEQ Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: This study presents an evaluation of the WeBarangay Local Government System, employing a dual-method approach that integrates quantitative and qualitative methodologies. Data is collected from a diverse participant pool through the application of the System Usability Scale (SUS) to measure usability and the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) to assess user experience. The findings reveal W eBarangay’ s exemplary usability, as evidenced by an outstanding average SUS score of 85.50, corresponding to an “Excellent” grade. Additionally, the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) unveils nuanced dimensions, emphasizing Attractiveness, Perspicuity, Efficiency, Dependability, Stimulation, and Novelty. The synthesis of SUS and UEQ findings identifies convergences and divergences, offering a comprehensive view of WeBarangay's performance. Commonalities and disparities between usability and user experience provide valuable insights, guiding targeted improvement efforts. The study's implications extend to practical enhancements in WeBarangay, ensuring user satisfaction and positive overall experiences. Ultimately, this research contributes to advancing fingerprint identification systems by emphasizing the integration of usability and user experience considerations in system development.

articleTitle: End-to-End Optical Layer Slicing Technology in Multi-Format Power Communication Optical Networks of SDH and OTN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: With the increasing number of transmission and distribution networks, end-to-end optical layer slicing is expected to provide a more efficient transmission method for power communication networks. However, the coexistence of multiple communication systems such as synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) and optical transport network (OTN) in current power communication networks poses challenges for end-to-end optical layer slicing. In this paper, against the backdrop of power communication networks where SDH and OTN communication systems coexist, we analyze the differences between SDH and OTN communication systems and consider two types of requests: bandwidth-constrained and latency-constrained. We construct an integer linear programming (ILP) model for slicing mapping and design a slicing request mapping strategy based on consistent transmission bandwidth and another slicing request mapping strategy based on minimal transmission latency. Surrounding the proposed content, we design simulation evaluation metrics for the two strategies and compare their performance with traditional strategies. We evaluate and discuss the effectiveness and efficiency of the two proposed strategies, providing a reference solution for the integration research of power communication networks under multiple communication systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Trust & Risk Based Access Control, in Autonomous Vehicles, by Using Ethereum vs Hyperledger Platforms Consensus Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Blockchain is an emerging technology for data security, integrity and secure communication in the networks of autonomous vehicles (AVs), this technology is extremely utilized for the AV s applications to record the access control data. The aim of this work is to share the knowledge on the growing demand of blockchain technology for the autonomous vehicles, discuss the consequences of integration of blockchain technology in AVs networks and access control systems for autonomous vehicles. This work offers a comprehensive investigation of existing applications for AVs based on blockchain technology with respect to various aspects including secure communication channels, forensics applications, secure data storage, reputation and trust management, data integrity and privacy. This work also offers an extensive study on various types of consensus algorithms used in Ethereum/Hyperledger, and provides a comprehensive comparison of trust and risk based on blockchain consensus algorithms on Ethereum over Hyperledger for autonomous vehicle applications.

articleTitle: Exploring SSL Enhancements Through Triplet-Based Representation Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In the research area of machine learning, self-supervised learning (SSL) strategies have demonstrated substantial promise in harnessing the vast pools of unlabeled data. This study presents the Barlow Triplets method, an SSL strategy that builds on the Barlow Twins framework to address its limitations in complex and diverse datasets. Our method enhances representation learning by introducing an additional augmented view through a triplet-based mechanism, which refines feature interactions and balances redundancy reduction with feature invariance. We employed an adapted loss function and validated our approach through experiments on the CIFAR10 dataset using a KNN classifier. Results show that Barlow Triplets surpasses traditional SSL methods, including Barlow Twins predecessor, across accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores, demonstrating its potential for practical applications and scalability. We compare two key formulations of Barlow Triplets, one of which is reported here for the first time. Our method requires fewer computational resources while achieving commendable performance. This research aims to contribute to SSL by introducing a method that seeks to optimize performance while potentially maintaining computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Intelligent Recognition of Leakage Infrared Thermal Imaging of Embankment Dams Based on ResNet Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: With the development of modern water conservancy, the leakage potential of embankment dams has received more and more attention. However, the current mainstream detection method is still manual inspection, which is often accompanied by high cost, time-consuming, damaging, and dangerous defects. How to effectively and accurately detect the leakage potential is of great significance for the prevention and control of floods and the overall safety monitoring of dykes. In response to the above urgent needs, this paper builds an intelligent identification system of infrared thermal imaging of levee leakage based on the ResNet network. The system takes the actual earth and stone embankment dam as the structural prototype and builds an indoor simulation model of the embankment dam. The infrared thermography spectral data of the embankment dam are collected using an infrared thermography camera. A ResNet network is used to classify and train the data-enhanced infrared image data to achieve the detection of leakage potentials of the embankment dam. The maximum accuracy of the ResNet network under two sample divisions can reach 99.9%, and the anomalous fluctuation in the test is small. Further, based on the accuracy optimal classification model, the leakage prediction is carried out on the real-time captured images of the acquired infrared thermal imager, and the prediction results are displayed in real-time. The results show that the system can achieve correct, efficient, and real-time detection of dam leakage. The proposed infrared thermal imaging intelligent identification system for dam leakage improves the identification efficiency of dam leakage and ensures classification accuracy, which provides a reference for scientific and safe dike defense.

articleTitle: Drone Position Estimation Based on Multipath Utilization in Urban Single Building NLOS Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The detection and localization of low-speed small drones in complex urban single-building environments is challenging. The presence of buildings will cause radar signals to reflect and refract, resulting in a large number of multipath signals. These multipath signals can interfere with drone detection and localization. Effective use of multipath signals to locate drone targets in urban single building environments is of great research significance. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a method that uses the multi-path effect of single-station radar electromagnetic waves to detect and locate drones in the non-line-of-sight (NLOS) range with known building layout information. First, a multipath echo signal model under non-line-of-sight conditions was constructed, and then a positioning solution algorithm using multipath signals in a single building scene was proposed. Finally, the proposed algorithm is verified using simulation and actual measurement data. Experimental results show that the positioning error of this method for micro-moving drone targets is less than 0.5m. In addition, the trajectory positioning result of the drone's moving target is very close to its actual movement trajectory.

articleTitle: Optimization of Cultural Heritage Protection Patrol Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Algorithms are commonly used to generate patrol routes. However, in cultural heritage protection patrols, traditional route planning methods often neglect the specific security requirements of cultural artifacts. Thus, there is a need for a specialized route planning algorithm and evaluation method tailored for cultural heritage protection to enhance security. This study proposes a method to optimize cultural heritage protection patrols, utilizing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) for comprehensive evaluation of pre-patrol route planning, actual patrol effectiveness, and patrol costs.During the pre-patrol route planning phase, to prevent the predictability of patrol routes and mitigate risks to cultural artifacts, this study employs an enhanced ant colony algorithm to generate multiple routes. It evaluates factors such as route differentiation and coverage of key patrol points, determining multiple patrol schemes based on these evaluations. To assess actual patrol effectiveness, the study analyzes patrol personnel GPS trajectories and extracts critical information. This optimization approach employs multidimensional quantitative analysis of the entire patrol system to enhance the efficiency and security of cultural heritage protection patrols.

articleTitle: Anomaly Intrusion Detection Algorithm Based on Distributed Fiber Optic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In the field of cultural heritage preservation, distributed fiber optic sensors are widely adopted for their long transmission distances, minimal loss, and suitability for long-distance monitoring. They are frequently used to monitor large perimeter intrusion events. Traditional intrusion detection methods are typically employed in fixed scenes without considering weather conditions. In volatile situations, these methods often exhibit lower recognition rates for human and mechanical disturbances and higher false alarm rates. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an anomaly intrusion detection algorithm, CCL-DCT-ST, integrating weather information. The main contributions are as follows: considering weather information in experimental monitoring scenarios, proposing a CCL detection model, and integrating a DCT-ST dynamic confidence threshold self-training strategy to identify abnormal intrusions effectively. Experimental results demonstrate a 25% improvement in accuracy on the dataset used in this study with the effective utilization of weather information. Moreover, implementing the DCT-ST semi-supervised strategy shows significant accuracy improvements on unlabeled datasets across various scenarios, thereby reducing false alarms from distributed fiber optic sensors.”

articleTitle: A Reasoning Method for Emergency Disposition Measures of Cultural Relics Safety Incidents Based on the Generalization-Generation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Emergency response decision-making is a core element in addressing unexpected safety incidents at various cultural heritage sites. Existing emergency plans often face challenges such as dispersed information, lack of integration, and high decision-making costs. To address these issues, this study proposes a reasoning method for emergency response measures to unexpected cultural heritage safety incidents based on the Generalization-Generation Pattern. This method first applies grounded theory, combined with large models, to efficiently and accurately extract key information from unstructured texts to construct a structured knowledge graph, promoting information sharing and supporting the reasoning of emergency response measures and optimizing resource allocation. Finally, by using the trained Generalization-Generation Pattern, we can predict response measures for cultural heritage safety incidents and analyze common patterns in similar situations, providing decision support for similar events. In practical applications at demonstration sites, this pattern has successfully provided reasonable response recommendations for specific safety incidents, demonstrating its potential in improving emergency response efficiency and reducing decision-making costs.

articleTitle: Using Software-Defined Tenant to Improve Network Adaptation in 5G Core Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Since the number of mobile network users are getting growth at a fast pace, more and more real-time and instant interaction applications of user equipment require high-quality 5G transmission. To satisfy diverse conditions from time-to-time, network service providers have to gain control capability to contribute to those innovative requirements. Hence, this paper proposed an idea of using software-defined networking (SDN) with tenants to improve scheduling and coordination. It splits management functions to different regional controllers for distributing cost, enabling load balancing, and allocating tenants. By leveraging SDN to enhance the flow control in 5G core network, this research introduced a reference design that aims to increase the network quality and stability.

articleTitle: Dynamic Tucker Decomposition for Traffic Data Completion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The missing data issue is common in practical traffic data collection, making accurate completion critical for various applications such as transport planning and route navigation. A lot of approaches have been proposed to address this issue, but many challenges remain, especially in designing efficient online completion algorithms that adapt to the streaming nature of traffic data. In this paper, to jointly aggregate multidimensional correlations, we utilize streaming tensors to represent traffic data and propose a dynamic tensor completion model based on Tucker decomposition to estimate missing values. Furthermore, we develop an efficient online algorithm to track the optimal core tensor and factor matrices, thanks to an alternating optimization framework. Experiments are conducted on two public traffic datasets to evaluate our method against some state-of-the-art baseline approaches. The results show that our method achieves completion performance closer to that of non-dynamic methods in a running time close to that of dynamic methods.

articleTitle: FSAH: Fast Specific Average Hashing for Cross-Modal Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Supervised Hashing-based methods for cross-modal retrieval have gained much attention in recent years due to their benefits in storage and computational efficiency. Many existing methods typically learn hash code shared by multiple modalities using pairwise similarity matrix of data, while preserving semantic similarity between heterogeneous modalities in a common hamming space. Although these approaches had achieved encouraging performance, there are still several drawbacks. 1) These methods cannot effectively preserve and combine the distinguishable modality-specific feature and heterogeneous similarity. 2) The computational complexity of the model using the similarity matrix is prohibitively high, which makes these models unscalable to large-scale datasets. 3) Methods that directly project the cross-modal data into a common latent space are unreasonable since data from different modalities have diverse structures and properties. In this paper, we proposed an innovative Fast Specific Average Hashing method for cross-modal retrieval, i.e. FSAH. Extensive experiments conducted on widely used benchmark database demonstrate that the proposed methods outperform state-of-the-art cross-modal hashing methods.

articleTitle: Unambiguous Direction Estimation Algorithm Using Dual Antennas in Cooperative Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The realization of anchor-free collaborative positioning requires accurate estimation of the direction of the incident wave from the neighboring collaborative nodes. The traditional passive direction-finding system requires at least three antennas to form an array to receive signals to achieve a high angular resolution, and phase ambiguity must be considered, which makes the system structure complex and costly. In response to this, the letter proposes an unambiguous direction-finding algorithm that can achieve high accuracy with only two antennas. This method uses a similar idea to synthetic aperture radar (SAR) to detect the direction. First, the wireless channel ratio of the two antennas is used to eliminate the phase difference between independent transceiver devices, and then the SAR formula is used to spatially filter the received data, and finally the direction information is obtained from the peak of the spatial spectrum. Software simulation and experimental verification show that the algorithm can achieve unambiguous estimation of multiple incoming wave directions, while reducing the clock synchronization requirements, and the measured direction-finding accuracy is basically within 1°.

articleTitle: CrackSAM: Study on Few-Shot Segmentation of Mural Crack Images Using SAM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Due to the scarcity of mural disease data and the complexity of mural backgrounds, Traditional deep learning image segmentation requires a large amount of annotated data for training, which limits its segmentation performance. Although the SAM (Segment Anything Model) excels in natural image segmentation with its zero-shot segmentation capabilities and geometric prompts, it performs poorly in segmenting mural cracks and requires manual input prompts during the inference stage. This study proposes an novel mural crack segmentation method, CrackSAM. First, the high-performance image encoder from the SAM model is used to generate image embedding feature maps of the input images. Next, our designed feature extraction module further refines these features, enhancing the model's ability to capture crack details. Then, a decoder module upsamples and decodes the refined features to generate highresolution segmentation masks. This process ensures the accuracy of the segmentation results. In experiments, even with only a small amount of public crack datasets for training, our method demonstrates performance close to specialized crack segmentation networks trained on full datasets. Notably, on our self-constructed mural crack dataset, the method effectively distinguishes and segments cracks in complex backgrounds, proving its potential and effectiveness in practical applications.
