This achievement provides a new technical approach for the automated segmentation and assessment of mural damages.

articleTitle: Research on Trajectory Planning Using Improved Harris Hawk Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: This paper investigates the trajectory planning problem of Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in complex urban environments. Addressing the limitations of traditional trajectory planning methods, which often get trapped in local optima and fail to meet practical flight requirements in complex and constrained environments, the study proposes a research approach based on the improved Harris's hawk optimization algorithm. Specifically, to enhance the algorithm's performance, the study first addresses issues related to the lack of diversity in the initial population and susceptibility to local optima by introducing a Gaussian distribution-based initialization method. Secondly, to balance the exploration and exploitation of the search space, a strategy based on a non-linearly decreasing function for updating escape energy is proposed. Experimental results demonstrate the algorithm's superiority in trajectory planning, significantly improving UAV flight efficiency and path planning accuracy, showing promising prospects for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: A Heterogeneous Device Access Gateway for Cultural Heritage Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: In the realm of cultural heritage protection, the use of disparate communication protocols and platforms by devices from various manufacturers hinders the integration of heterogeneous device data onto a unified platform. Current heterogeneous device gateways demand high operational skills and prior technical preparation. To counter these challenges, this paper presents the design and implementation of a security-oriented heterogeneous device gateway for cultural relics. The gateway consolidates critical modules such as data collection, caching, protocol identification, and data parsing, addressing the technical difficulties in integrating heterogeneous device data. It employs an innovative “learn-then-connect” approach, adapting to and efficiently parsing data from various devices by learning their communication protocols and formats. Experimental simulations collected data from five types of heterogeneous devices, amassing 2,500 entries. The results demonstrate the gateway's capability to effectively identify and parse the communication protocols of reconnected devices.

articleTitle: Effectiveness Evaluation of Battlefield Airspace Control Information System under the Dynamic Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Battlefield airspace control information system (BACIS) is an information system for unified planning and control of various air activities, and the evaluation of its system effectiveness is of great importance for the complete realization of the functions and efficient and reliable operation of BACIS. In this paper, on the basis of constructing the dynamic selection-based system of information system effectiveness evaluation indicators, we determine the weights of the indicators and the weights of the evaluation time points based on the subjective and objective information and the variance minimization method, respectively, and generate the results of the dynamic evaluation of the information system effectiveness with the introduction of the time dimension.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Neural Network Based Graph Theory for EEG Classification of Motor Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used due to their high temporal resolution. However, accurate classification remains a challenge due to the non-stationary nature of the EEG and the complexity of feature extraction. This study presents a convolutional neural network based graph theory to improve the classification accuracy of motor imagery (MI) EEG. Graph theory is used to construct spatial relationship models between EEG electrodes. Neural networks are used for classification, and residual connections are added to address node similarity issues that arise with increasing network complexity. The experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement in classification accuracy compared to the traditional method. Specifically, the accuracy of the test dataset exceeds 70.83% while also reducing computational complexity. These results demonstrate the robustness and generalize ability of the method. The proposed method achieves superior classification accuracy compared to existing techniques through graph theory algorithms and residual connections for EEG-based BCI. This study presents a method for improving the classification accuracy of MI tasks using EEG. The combination of graph theory algorithms and residual connections provides a promising avenue for future research in this field, allowing for more accurate and reliable BCI technologies.

articleTitle: Design of Fruit Quality Recognition System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The process of fruit picking by intelligent robots requires the screening of the fruit's appearance. A digital image processing algorithm is proposed to comprehensively analyze and evaluate the fruit's appearance information, including size and color. This analysis is then combined with flexible transmission methods to effectively classify the fruits. The system is controlled by two masters, with Raspberry PI serving as the upper computer for image information acquisition and processing, VNC remote connection, and human-computer interface. The other system is the STM32 minimal system, which is equipped with FreeRTOS for motor and lamp control, temperature and humidity acquisition, as well as system information display. It efficiently accomplishes the task of fruit recognition and classification with speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: An Image Denoising Method Based on Swin Transformer V2 and U-Net Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: To address the issue of image degradation caused by noise during image acquisition and transmission, this paper proposes ST2CFNet, an image denoising model based on Swin Transformer V2. This model innovatively integrates Swin Transformer V2 into a U-Net architecture to fill the current research gap related to the application of Swin Transformer V2 in image denoising. The model's dual-branch mechanism of Transformer and local convolution efficiently extracts and combines the long-distance pixel correlations and local feature information of images, preserving more image details. A multi-feature fusion module is designed to learn more beneficial knowledge for image denoising from features across multiple layers of the network. To enhance convergence speed, adaptive adjustments were made to the Swin Transformer V2 block, effectively stabilizing and improving the training outcomes. Experimental comparisons with several popular image denoising methods demonstrate that this approach outperforms local convolution-based methods in terms of average peak signal-to-noise ratio and offers lower fioating-point operations compared to similarly effective Transformer-based methods, indicating that the model can significantly enhance inference efficiency while preserving more image details.

articleTitle: Angelarium: Integrating IoT and AI for Optimal Angel Fish Habitat Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 16th International Conference on Advanced Infocomm Technology (ICAIT)
abstract: The popularity of aquarium hobbyism has spurred advancements in technology aimed at enhancing the care and management of aquatic ecosystems. This study introduces Angelarium, an innovative system integrating the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to optimize the habitat conditions of Angel Fish (Pterophyllum scalare) in home aquariums. By leveraging IoT sensors for realtime monitoring of water quality parameters and AI algorithms for automated feeding and anomaly detection, Angelarium aims to streamline maintenance tasks and ensure optimal conditions for fish health. The study focuses on the development, implementation, and evaluation of Angelarium, including the creation of a user-friendly mobile application for remote aquarium management. Through comprehensive testing and user feedback, the effectiveness and usability of Angelarium are assessed, highlighting its potential to revolutionize ornamental fishkeeping practices. This research contributes to the intersection of IoT, AI, and aquatic biology, fostering sustainable and technologically advanced solutions for aquarium enthusiasts.
